title: Whose Defaults These Are
description: Explain where a model's biases come from and what that predicts about its output on cases the training data underrepresented — from the demographics baked into training text to the assumed defaults an AI tool writes straight into your code.

title: What Leaves Your Hands When You Type It
description: Decide what is and isn't safe to send to a third-party AI tool, and why — from where a prompt physically goes after you hit send, to a personal rule you'll actually apply under deadline pressure.

title: Whose Work This Was Built On
description: Explain the labor and attribution questions behind AI-generated output — the uncompensated training corpus and the paid-but-outsourced feedback labeling behind it — and where your own responsibility to disclose AI involvement actually begins.

title: What Happens When You Can't Access It
description: Assess your own dependence on AI tools and plan for the failure modes: outages, price and access changes, and the specific skills that quietly erode when a tool does a task for you every single time.

title: A Working Ethics, Not a Poster
description: Apply everything in this phase — bias and defaults, privacy, disclosure and attribution, and dependence — to one real, specific AI-assisted work decision, and defend the call you made when the concerns actually conflict.
